The API died because the disk filled up: a `report-export` job wrote about 20 GB to `/var/lib/stockroom/exports` and left Postgres no room to write, and the API was still down when the log ends at 05:29:57.

The log's dates are 2026-03-09, so check this is the night you mean.

1. From 03:05:00 to 03:12:48 `report-export` wrote 40 CSV parts of 512 MB each, one every 12 seconds.
2. The disk warning for `/var/lib/stockroom` fired at 91% at 03:09:03 and at 99% at 03:13:30.
3. At 03:14:00 the db logged `could not extend file "base/16384/2619": No space left on device`.
4. At 03:14:03 the api aborted its transaction and shut down its worker pool, then exited with status 1 at 03:14:06.
5. From 03:16:00 to 03:28:00 at least, the proxy logged `upstream api refused connection` every two minutes, and the log has no api line of any kind after the exit. `web` and `proxy` kept serving 200s throughout.

The `cache: slow command` warnings run all night at the same rate before and after, so they look unrelated.

To recover, free space by moving or deleting the `part-*.csv` files in `/var/lib/stockroom/exports`, confirm Postgres is healthy, then start the api. It has `restart: unless-stopped` in `docker-compose.yml`, yet the log shows no restart attempts, so find out why it stayed down.

To stop a repeat, get the exports off the database's volume or cap the job's output. Nothing in this repo defines `report-export`, so I couldn't see what launched it or why it wrote that much.
